findings.title: The generic orbitGraph loop (values beyond 2^53) can report truncated for a search that ends with exactly cap positions and the whole suite stays green (surviving M14 on the second search loop)
findings.location: packages/engine/src/search.ts:320 (the generic loop's final return); packages/engine/test/unit/mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts:313-356 (the handover cases never end with exactly cap items)
findings.claim: Since the residual fix for P3-RT-07-02, orbitGraph has two search loops. The suite pins the cap boundary of SPEC 5.5 only on the search on numbers (F10, the fast-path M14, is caught). The generic loop, which runs once a value leaves the safe range, can say truncated true at the natural end of a search with exactly cap items, and no test notices.
findings.expected: SPEC 5.5: the cap acts only 'when the search is about to add one position more than the cap'. A search that finds exactly cap positions ends with truncated false on either loop, and some test runs the generic loop at cap equal to the orbit size.
findings.observed: With redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch applied, `npx vitest run --project engine` exits 0 (65 files, 2218 tests). The full `npm test` set gives 133 files passing. The other two files, T03.test.ts and T11.test.ts, hit Vitest's 5 s limit at load 12 and pass when rerun under the patch (exit 0). The proposed test packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-11-generic-cap.test.ts fails 2 of 2 under the patch and passes without it. It runs A2, B2, G2 and A3 orbits and triangle layer bounds with the seeds times 2^60 against the same search on the plain seeds, at cap n-1, n and n+1.
findings.reproduction: From this branch (b9b8504 plus dfb1716) after `npm ci --prefer-offline`: `patch -p1 < redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch && npx vitest run --project engine --exclude '**/redteam-*'; echo exit=$?` gives exit=0. Then `npx vitest run --project engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-11-generic-cap.test.ts; echo exit=$?` gives exit=1. `patch -R -p1 < redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch` and the same file passes.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 5.5 'Order and truncation of a search'; RT-11 attack 31 (surviving M14 is major); SPEC 7.7 Engine golden row; CONTRACTS.md 3
findings.proposedFix: Adopt redteam-RT-11-generic-cap.test.ts, which compares the generic loop on scaled seeds with the search on numbers on the plain seeds at the cap boundary. Also add a cap equal to the orbit size to the handover cases of mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts.

findings.title: The 25 ms orbit benchmark of SPEC 7.6 no longer measures Big arithmetic: the bigint loop can become 30 times slower and orbit.bench.ts stays green
findings.location: packages/engine/test/bench/orbit.bench.ts:38-64 (seeds 0 and 1 on a Big board); packages/engine/src/search.ts:289-297 (searchOnNumbers taken on every SafeInt or Big board while values are safe)
findings.claim: The residual fix for P3-RT-07-02 made orbitGraph search on plain numbers while every value is a safe integer. The SPEC 7.6 benchmark, '2000 positions on a board with 12 nodes in Big arithmetic', still seeds 0 and 1 and so now times the numbers path. The bigint loop with decimal keys, which it timed at G3 (19.75 to 21.60 ms, and 21.01 ms at the gate, per DECISIONS.md), now runs only for values beyond 2^53, and nothing times it. No decisions entry records this change of what the benchmark measures.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.6 'Main-thread work': the worst case of E-9, 2000 positions on a 12-node board in Big arithmetic, is repeated by a Vitest benchmark that fails above 25 ms (median of seven). RT-11 attack 24 requires that 'the arithmetic is Big and not SafeInt or number'.
findings.observed: redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F9-generic-slow.patch adds 20 microseconds to each move of the bigint loop only. Under it, orbit.bench.ts passes at a median of 11.11 ms (load 4.1) and 7.84 ms (load 11), while the same board, cap 2000 and maxDepth 40 with the seeds times 2^60 (the same 2000 positions, same parents) takes 312.35 ms and 340.10 ms in redteam-RT-11-big-values.bench.ts. Unmutated at load 5.6 to 6: orbit.bench.ts 11.09 ms; seeds 0/1 2.91 ms; the seeds times 2^60 (the bigint loop) 21.68 ms. At load 11, the times-2^60 case measured 27.74 to 39.92 ms against 25. With the search loop as it was before b85ac0f restored (R-b85ac0f-search.patch, load 11), seeds 0/1 take 13.19 and 13.66 ms in bigint. The machine was never quiet (load 4 to 18), so absolute medians are indicative only. The F9 result does not depend on load.
findings.reproduction: After `npm ci --prefer-offline` on this branch: `bash redteam/rt11-p4/bench-mutant.sh "$PWD" redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F9-generic-slow.patch`. It applies the patch, runs `npx vitest run --config test/bench/vitest.config.ts` in packages/engine, reverts, and prints the medians: orbit benchmark under 25 ms and passing; RT-11 bench at over 300 ms and failing. Or by hand: `patch -p1 < redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F9-generic-slow.patch`, then in packages/engine `npx vitest run --config test/bench/vitest.config.ts orbit.bench; echo exit=$?` gives exit=0 and `npx vitest run --config test/bench/vitest.config.ts redteam-RT-11; echo exit=$?` gives exit=1.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 'Main-thread work' (the benchmark sentence); SPEC 5.5 'Orbits' (the 9 ms Big measurement it repeats); SPEC 5.1 E-9; RT-11 attack 24; CONTRACTS.md 3 (the benchmark: 'Big, median of seven runs, fails above 25 ms')
findings.proposedFix: Make the 7.6 benchmark time the bigint loop, for example with the unit seeds times 2^60, which give the same 2000 positions. Or time both loops, each against 25 ms (redteam-RT-11-big-values.bench.ts does this). Record in DECISIONS.md which arithmetic the benchmark measures.

findings.title: T15.spec.ts checks the A-3 node names with a wildcard for the city number (residual sibling of P3-RT-11-08)
findings.claim: The only check of T15's node names (A-3) accepts any digit as the city label and does not tie it to the button's data-node. T15 buttons that all said 'City 1, ...', or carried wrong labels, would pass.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.5 A-3 fixes the name template ('City 2, population 1, mutation would raise it'). Each button's name should be compared whole, with the label read from its data-node, as P3-RT-11-08's fix did for A-4 sentences.
findings.observed: `expect(await b.getAttribute('aria-label')).toMatch(/^City \d, population 1, mutation would change nothing$/)` runs in a loop over the four buttons of the square. No exact 'City <n>, ...' name appears anywhere in T15.spec.ts.
findings.reproduction: `grep -n 'toMatch(/^City' site/tests/e2e/T15.spec.ts` prints line 132 as quoted. `grep -nE "'City [0-9], " site/tests/e2e/T15.spec.ts` prints nothing.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.5 A-3; CONTRACTS.md 5.3; RT-11 attack 33 (a loose comparison of a fixed sentence is minor per file)
findings.proposedFix: Inside the loop, read data-node and compare toHaveAttribute('aria-label', `City ${label}, population 1, mutation would change nothing`).

notes: C1 (classByMinors never falls back to the bigint elimination) survives every test. I believe it is equivalent on the engine's domain. The class only needs the signs of the leading minors. On a balanced connected matrix with entries large enough for products to pass 2^53, the class is always indefinite, and the first non-positive minor is hugely negative. In 300000 random balanced connected 2-to-8-node matrices with entries up to about 2^34, the double and bigint eliminations never disagreed (redteam/rt11-p4/rt11_minors_search.mjs; 12672 finite, 6050 affine). The test comment that 'only the bigint elimination is exact there' is true of the values, not of the class.
F4 (the generic loop fires a node holding 0 under legalOnly) is equivalent: firing a 0 leaves the position unchanged, the key already exists, and the move is skipped.

phaseInForce reads `^\s*phase:\s*(\d+),` from site/src/tools/registry/T*.ts.
